The '''MetaWatch''' is a brand name of discontinued [[smartwatch]]es developed by Meta Watch, Ltd. '''Strata MetaWatch''' and '''Frame MetaWatch''' are digital smartwatches released in 2012, funded by raising money via the [[crowd funding]] platform [[Kickstarter]].<ref name="kickstarter">{{cite web|url=http://www.kickstarter.com/projects/metawatch/metawatch-strata-the-smartwatch-for-the-iphone-4s|title=MetaWatch STRATA: the Smartwatch for the iPhone 4S & Android|work=Kickstarter}}</ref> MetaWatch was a company founded by former [[Fossil Group|Fossil]] engineers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/9/3/6102183/meta-watch-meta-m1-smartwatch-review|title= Meta Watch Meta M1 review: the watchmaker's smartwatch |work= TheVerge|date= 3 September 2014 }}</ref>

== History ==
The first generation of MetaWatch watches was released as a development system in September 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2011/08/25/fossils-meta-watch-passes-the-fcc-your-magic-wristwatch-fantas/|title=Fossil's Meta Watch passes the FCC, your magic wristwatch fantasies are about to come true|author=Daniel Cooper|publisher=AOL|work=Engadget}}</ref> Two models were sold - analog with [[OLED]] displays (model WDS111, style AU1000) and fully digital (model WDS112, style AU2000). Both were provided with a clip for charging, flashing, and debugging.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://metawatch.org/assets/images/developers/MetaWatch_Reflash_your_Watch_Firmware_2.0.pdf|title=META WATCH REFLASH YOUR WATCH FIRMWARE|website=metawatch.org}}</ref> For wireless connection, [[Bluetooth]] 2.1 is used via a TI CC2560 module.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dpin.de/~nils/metawatch.html|title=MetaWatch Hacking|work=dpin.de}}</ref> As a serial RAM [[Integrated circuit|Microchip]] 23A640 serial is used.

Unofficial first and half generation was extended of Bluetooth 4.0 capability. Style numbers for these watches were AU2001 and AU2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://metawatch.org/forums/thread/467/questions-about-new-model#dis-post-3010|title=Metawatch - Questions about new model|author=MODX Systems, LLC|work=metawatch.org}}</ref><ref name="model_style">{{cite web|url=http://www.metawatch.org/forums/thread/624/any-differences-internally-between-au2001-au2004#dis-post-4409|title=Metawatch - Any differences internally between AU2001 & AU2004?|author=MODX Systems, LLC|work=metawatch.org}}</ref>

The second generation of MetaWatch had Bluetooth 4.0, a KXTI9 [[accelerometer]] instead of KXTF9 (using less active power), and larger battery. The 4 pins on the back of the case were multiplexed and could be either used with [[Spy-Bi-Wire]] (serialized version of [[JTAG]]) or serial out/ground. External serial [[Random-access memory|RAM]] was larger. The clip provided with watches was for charging and reflash only. A JTAG clip for development could be bought separately.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metawatch.org/forums/thread/637/metawatch-store|title=Metawatch - Metawatch Store|author=MODX Systems, LLC|work=metawatch.org}}</ref>

The company has since ceased operations.

== Models ==
Second generation watches were sold under names Strata (model code SW12-1) and Frame (model code SW12-2). Strata has [[Water Resistant mark|Water Resistant Mark]] 5 and Frame has Water Resistant Mark 3.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.metawatch.com/models/ |title=MetaWatch Smartwatch - Models |access-date=2013-05-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130621130729/http://www.metawatch.com/models/ |archive-date=2013-06-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Strata, which was focused more on value, was bulkier but more durable with its double injection-moulded [[polyurethane]] body.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.trustedreviews.com/reviews/metawatch-strata|title=MetaWatch Strata Review {{!}} Trusted Reviews|last=Kelly|first=Gordon|date=June 17, 2013|work=Trusted Reviews|access-date=2018-09-21|language=en-US}}</ref>  It was also cheaper as the Kare model retailed for $140.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.theverge.com/2012/7/27/3174393/metawatch-strata-smartwatch-kickstarter|title=MetaWatch introduces Strata smartwatch on Kickstarter: 'iOS 6 made it possible'|last=Ziegler|first=Chris|date=July 27, 2012|work=The Verge|access-date=2018-09-21}}</ref> The Frame, on the other hand, was the variant targeted towards the fashion segment. The device featured a slimmer [[stainless steel]] build, smaller display, [[leather]] bands and a price tag of $199.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pcworld.com/article/2030093/review-the-metawatch-frame-is-a-very-cool-smartwatch.html|title=Review: The MetaWatch Frame is a very cool smartwatch|last=Friedman|first=Lex|date=March 13, 2013|work=PCWorld|access-date=2018-09-21|language=en}}</ref>  The Strata model was initially offered as an [[iOS]]-only device due to challenges in developing a version for the [[Android (operating system)|Android]] platform.<ref name=":0" /> An Android-compatible version was later released.

In 2014, Metawatch announced Meta M1,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/arieladams/2014/09/17/meta-watch-m1-smartwatch-frank-nuovo/#28dbbc475cfa|title=From Geek To Chic: The Meta Watch M1 Smartwatch By Frank Nuovo|last=Adams|first=Ariel|work=Forbes|access-date=2018-09-22|language=en}}</ref> a premium smartwatch developed in collaboration with [[Frank Nuovo]]. The designer was known for his iconic works at [[Vertu]] and [[Nokia]], where he served as a Vice President and Chief of Design. The device was launched at the 2014 [[Consumer Electronics Show]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/mobile/metawatch-launches-meta-smartwatch-brand/|title=MetaWatch unveils new high-end smartwatch by former Vertu designer|last=Mogg|first=Trevor|date=2014-01-06|work=Digital Trends|access-date=2018-09-22|language=en-US}}</ref>
